## 1.9.0

Terminal 1.9: gear is found and grouped by its bonus, by area type ("biome") or against a creature type, alone or with
the rest of a search; `@loot`'s items are read for bonuses in the background; `.pick` picks someone of your group with
a roll of names; and Terminal no longer relies on the layer or the realm name WoW Forever's November 20 hotfix hid.
With the fixes of a bug, quality, consistency and speed pass.

**Bonus search** (the player: WoW Forever's items with effects by area type, "biome", or against a creature type)
- `bonus:` finds gear by its bonus, read from the item's own tooltip (the game's English text): where it grows,
  `bonus:haunted`, `bonus:swamp`, `bonus:stronghold` (the ten area types; `bonus:area`: any), or what it's against,
  `bonus:undead`, `bonus:beast`, `bonus:troll` (the creature types and the species tooltips name; `bonus:creature`:
  any). `is:bonus` is either. Wordings read: "This effect is doubled in Marsh and Swamp areas", "Increases Spirit by
  16 in Cavernous or Underground areas", "+45 Attack Power when fighting Undead", "against the Naga", set bonuses too.
- `| group by bonus` (also on the bar's Group menu) makes a group per bonus, "Haunted", "Against Undead"; an item with
  two is in both. Enter on a group lists it with its `bonus:` filter.
- Simple mode: "haunted bonus", "haunted gear", "gear for swamp areas", "against undead", "vs beasts", "biome gear",
  "items by bonus". An area type's word alone stays a name ("Volcanic Leggings"). Explained as "with a Haunted bonus".
- Which area types you're standing in isn't answered: the game doesn't say, and which zones are which isn't published.

**Bonuses combine with the rest of a search** (the player: "faction or reputation rewards that deal 2x damage to
trolls, or have a bonus in mountainous areas")
- A faction's rewards take a bonus said in plain words: "argent dawn rewards against trolls", "reputation rewards that
  deal 2x damage to trolls", "faction rewards with a bonus in mountainous areas", "exalted rewards against undead".
  In Advanced syntax they're `@reputation is:reward argent dawn bonus:troll`; the title says the bonus too.
- The words a bonus is said with ("deal 2x damage", "with a bonus", "that have") are no longer searched as names, in
  any list: "trinkets that deal 2x damage to trolls" looks for trinkets with `bonus:troll`. "to trolls" and
  "fighting undead" are read as "against". Tab offers `bonus:`'s values after `@reputation` and `@itemset` too.

**Bonuses in `@loot`** (the player: "why can I not look at `@loot` that has bonuses against trolls / biome?")
- The game has a tooltip only for items it has loaded, and most of AtlasLoot's aren't. Items not loaded yet are now
  asked for in the background, a batch at a time (not in combat), and read as they come in; the search shown is put up
  again as they do, and the footer counts down how many are left ("reading 1,240 items' tooltips for bonuses").
- What was read is kept for the next session of the same client build, so the second time is instant; written at
  logout only when something new was read. A group of its own in `.saved` ("items' bonuses read from their
  tooltips"); `.saved clear bonuses` sticks.
- An item the server never answers is let go for the session (the search no longer ran again every 30 s, and the
  footer's note no longer stayed). In Simple mode, rows without the bonus aren't listed as "the closest" while
  tooltips are read. The game's item-loading event is listened for only while items are awaited.

**`.pick`** (the player: "I like the .pick idea!")
- `.pick` picks someone of your group at random ("who's buying the repairs"): their names roll by on screen, slower
  and slower, and land on the pick, and Terminal says it in the group's chat (party, raid, or instance chat when your
  group is the instance's) as the roll lands on it.
- `.pick quiet` keeps the pick to you. `.pick tacos, pizza, sushi` picks one of those (commas, or words without them);
  outside a group a list is only shown to you. A `.pick` run again mid-roll ends the first.
- While the game holds chat back from addons (an encounter in an instance), the pick is said only to you.
- `.random` and `.choose` say the same. It's a new file: restart the game for it.

**Your layer can't be told any more** (the player: "double check if layering values are undetectable anymore")
- WoW Forever's hotfix of November 20, 2026 hid the layer: every creature's GUID now carries a different server and
  zone number, two standing side by side included (measured by TitanLayer's author on 1.60.1.71037), and Blizzard said
  layer-picking addons would be stopped through API changes. `@layer` read that zone number, so it showed a different,
  meaningless layer for each creature you met.
- `@layer`, "what layer am i on" and "my layer" now say the game hides it, and no creature is read for it.

**Nothing relies on the realm's name** (the player: "fix anything that relies on realm name too")
- Since the same hotfix the game gives no realm name (`GetRealmName()` is empty). Character names are unique across
  Forever's realms, so Terminal goes by the name alone.
- Experience: your bag addon's alts, kept with a realm, are matched to their notes again, by the whole name (the first
  name only when one side has no surname); an alt forgotten with `.forget` before stays forgotten. No "-Realm" is put
  after a name any more (`@xp`, `@lockout`, `@mail` and its warning).
- Upgrades: your `.weights` picks and what each item is usable by are kept by your name; picks kept as `Name@Realm`
  are found again.
- Share: a Battle.net friend whose realm Battle.net still names is told apart by the server in the characters' GUIDs;
  OpenMap keys them once (two hellos, two dots on the map before).
- Console: `/etc/os-release` says "forever", not an empty realm.

**Fixed in the pass**
- With a few alts forgotten before, `@xp` listed nothing and `.forget` failed (the list was changed while walked).
- The bar's Group menu over `@loot` no longer reads a hundred tooltips to check Group by bonus; a `| bonus:x` step no
  longer makes a table per row; tooltip lines without a bonus's words aren't read. The speed check has two new cases.
- `.pick` offers "quiet" only as its first word; your `.weights` picks kept as `Name@Realm` are found when you clear
  your own weights too; the help, examples and docs say what 1.9 changed.

## 1.8.0

Terminal 1.8: Pawn's scales judge your upgrades, Terminal answers "how do I..." with its own help, faction rewards
are found and grouped by what they are, PvP quests track and untrack in one go, and what's new after an update waits
in the empty prompt; with the fixes of a release review.

**Pawn's scales judge upgrades** (a player on CurseForge)
- With Pawn installed, the scales it shows in its tooltips for your character judge `is:upgrade` ("upgrades", "quest
  upgrades", "vendor upgrades"), read as they are now: no exporting and pasting. Two scales shown: an item counts if
  it's an upgrade for either, and its tooltip says which ("An upgrade for: Pawn "Healer"").
- A tree or your own weights picked in `.weights` still come first; `.weights pawn` (or `.weights all`) goes back to
  Pawn's scales. OneForAll's gear value is used when neither Pawn nor `.weights` says. `.weights paste` opens a window
  to paste a Pawn scale string into, Pawn installed or not.
- `.weights` lists Pawn's scales with their weights; `.integrations` has a Pawn line. Read through the functions Pawn
  offers other addons; nothing of Pawn's is copied.

**"How do I...": Terminal's own help as search results**
- Ask "how do i send to party", "what does shift enter do", "how do i make my own command", "how can i change the
  theme": the topics your words name come up as rows, best first, each saying what to do in a line (its tooltip in
  full). Enter writes its example into the prompt; Shift+Left comes back. 25 topics, from sending to chat and filters
  to aliases, themes, tabs and `!t`.
- Answered only when every word fits a topic, so other questions keep their lines ("how many linen do i have", "how do
  i get the scarlet key", "how do i share quests"); "what does ___ do" answers keys and Terminal's commands, not a
  spell's or an item's name. In Simple mode it says things Simple mode's way, with no Advanced syntax.

**Faction rewards: found and grouped by what they are**
- A quartermaster's reward (OneForAll's, and AtlasLoot's faction loot) is found by its type and subtype as the game
  names them: `@faction cenarion tailoring` lists the Cenarion Circle's tailoring patterns, `@rep argent plate` the
  Argent Dawn's plate. It listed nothing before. `type:` filters them too: `@rep is:reward type:tailoring`.
- Group has a new choice, Category: Recipes, Weapons, Gear, Consumables, Pets, Mounts and Other, for any list of items
  (rewards, loot, your bags): `@rep is:reward | group by category`. Step into a group and Subtype splits it further:
  the recipes by profession (Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Tailoring...), gear by Cloth, Leather, Mail or Plate. Category
  takes Type's place in the menu (they said the same); `| group by type` still works typed, and shows in the menu.
- `type:pet` (companion and battle pets) and `type:mount` filter by them too.

**Track or untrack your PvP quests** (a player on CurseForge)
- "untrack pvp quests", "track pvp quests only", "track battleground quests": the PvP quests in your log, beside the
  dungeon, raid and class ones. A PvP quest is one the game tags PvP, one under a battleground's heading in your log
  (the game's own battleground names, in your client's language) or under "Battlegrounds", or, with QuestieDB, one
  whose zone is a battleground. `is:pvp` finds them too: `@quest is:pvp >>> untrack`.

**What's new, in the empty prompt**
- After an update the empty prompt's first suggestion is "try: .changelog (what's new in 1.8.0)": Enter on it opens
  the changelog, Shift+Right writes `.changelog`. Gone once the changelog is opened or you type over it; a fresh
  install gets the tour instead.

**And**
- The options panel has a "Keep your session" checkbox; it was only in "terminal settings" and `.set keepSession`.
- With Terminal bound to a chord whose key types a character (Ctrl+Space on clients where it types a space; Shift and
  a letter), that character is no longer typed into the prompt as it opens, while the chord is held (a player on
  CurseForge).
- With Baganator, your gold no longer lists a "Warband bank" at 0c: WoW Forever has none.
- `.report`'s last trace lines are plain text: one holding an item's link pasted its colour codes.
- New texts translated (German, French, Spanish, Russian, Chinese).

**Release review fixes**
- What's new: typed over and then emptied, the prompt showed it again (and Enter did nothing); once shown, Enter on
  an empty prompt opened the changelog even when it showed Share's invite.
- How-to questions took lines that weren't theirs ("how do i get the scarlet key", "what does fade do"); a how-to
  question cost about 24 times a plain search's ranking on each keystroke; Enter on two topics wrote a command a
  second Enter would have run (`.bind CTRL-SPACE`).
- Pawn: the tooltip named Pawn's scale only for `.weights` picks; with two or three scales shown every row was weighed
  once per scale; `.weights all` and the messages pointing at the paste window said what they did before Pawn.
- A chord's character was dropped even with the chord's keys let go, so a quick first space of your own was lost.
- On other clients the battle pets' family names ("Wasser") were Simple mode's words for `type:pet`.
- PvP quests: with no battleground named, the list was asked again for every quest on every quest log update.

**For add-on authors and testers**
- Every test file passes on its own, and the run fails a file that leaves the game's stand-ins, Terminal's settings,
  its lists or its window changed (`python tests/run_smoke.py <names>`, `--alone`); failures inside a file's checks
  are all counted. `tests/perf.py` checks what a fixed set of searches costs, in Lua instructions, against
  `tests/perf_baseline.json` (over 10% more fails). CI runs both.

## 1.7.0

Terminal 1.7: a new look (cropped, framed icons, Forever's parchment-white names, a quieter kind column, a frame with
some depth), and one answer everywhere: places that answered one question two ways (how a recipe is learned, can you
take a quest, when to train a profession's next rank, a faction's rewards, `!t` answers) now agree, with the fixes of a
release review.

**A new look**
- The result rows' icons are drawn the way the bags draw them: without the icon's own rough edge, in a thin frame, an
  item's in its quality colour from uncommon up.
- The Forever theme's names are parchment-white with the letters you typed in gold (they were white in gold names);
  details are a softer brown-grey. A Forever theme you never tuned takes the new colours; one you tuned stays.
- The kind column is quieter: each row's kind ("Spell", "Quest"...) in the details' colour after a small dot of its own
  colour, the selected row's in its colour; on one line, the column as wide as the longest kind's name in your font.
  The column was a rainbow beside the items' quality colours.
- When you asked for one kind (an `@kind` typed, a question such as "recipes i can learn now", a chain's step, a
  category you picked) and every row is of it, the kind column is hidden: the footer says what they are, and the names
  and details get its room. Plain searches keep it, so it never comes and goes as you type.
- The classic frame (the Forever, Horde and Alliance themes) has the game's stone grain over its colour, faint, and a
  shade darkening toward the bottom. The flat frame stays flat.

**How a recipe is learned: one answer**
- A recipe you don't know (`@recipe is:unknown`) and its "where to learn" are made from one record, so they say the
  same: the Merchant's Favor and its vendor ("Bought with 30 Merchant's Favor", the vendor's own row after it), a
  trainer (one whose window listed it, TrainerSpells' list, or a craft AtlasLoot knows with no recipe item and no
  Favor), and the recipe item with where to get it.
- Fixed: a Favor recipe AtlasLoot knows as a craft (Mrrggl Smrrthle) said "Trainer" on its row and listed trainers in
  "where to learn"; a Favor recipe that also has a recipe item left the Favor out; a recipe only TrainerSpells lists
  said "Trainer" and nothing in "where to learn"; a recipe whose only sellers serve the other faction says "Vendor (the
  other faction only)" on its row, as "where to learn" does.
- A recipe row is drawn in the colour `is:orange`, `is:yellow`, `is:green`, `is:grey` and `is:skillup` judge it by:
  your skill now, as the levelling plan does (they read the window's last colour, and the row was drawn in it). The
  rows are drawn again after a skill-up.

**Can you take a quest: one answer everywhere**
- "can i take ", `is:cantake` and `sort:cantake`, the quests for your level ("quests near me", the zones'
  counts), "quest upgrades" and the quests a standing opens judge a quest by the same rules: your race, class and side
  (a quest only the other faction's NPCs give isn't yours), its level, what it needs (a profession's skill, a
  standing) and what QuestieDB and OneForAll's prerequisites say stands in the way.
- `sort:cantake`'s detail says the level a quest needs, as "can i take" does.
- "What does  unlock" counts OneForAll's chains too, and names only the quest a step really leads to.

**Training a profession's next rank: one answer**
- "what should i do" and the prompt's examples decide the same way when it's time to train a profession's next rank:
  TrainerSpells' next rank when it's installed, else your skill at the top of a rank a trainer teaches past. Fishing,
  Cooking and First Aid at 150 aren't offered a trainer (their next rank is a book, then a quest).
- Both ask for a trainer who can teach that rank ("nearest expert tailoring trainer"): a Journeyman Tailor can't teach
  Expert and is left out, as "where to learn" leaves such trainers out. Any trainer search takes a rank the same way
  (`trainer:tailoring:expert`; apprentice, journeyman, expert or artisan).

**`!t` answers: the asker's, not yours**
- Your own Simple-mode Filter and Sort picks no longer apply to a guildie's `!t` question (with "Rare or better"
  picked, "!t nearest innkeeper" found nothing); they're still yours after.
- "around my level", "above my level" and every `lvl:me` in a `!t` question are the asker's level.

**A faction's rewards: one list**
- " > rewards" lists AtlasLoot's rewards OneForAll doesn't, as " rewards" and `@reputation
  is:reward` did: "Argent Dawn > rewards" left out the Mantles of the Dawn.
- A faction OneForAll says isn't in WoW Forever yet (Zandalar Tribe, Brood of Nozdormu, Hydraxian Waterlords) has no
  AtlasLoot rewards listed for it, on any client language.
- A reward's vendor on the map (Enter) is one who'll sell to you, the nearest to where you stand, as " > sources"
  lists them (it was the first OneForAll lists: the Argent Dawn's Hasana in Tirisfal, wherever you stood).

**Smaller answers made to agree**
- `is:upgrade` over `@loot` follows its rule for both addons' rows: loot from dungeons you can enter (OneForAll's quest
  rewards, crafted gear and reputation rewards could be "upgrades", AtlasLoot's never were).
- A boss's drop chance from OneForAll is never put on AtlasLoot's trash row, on any client language (it hid AtlasLoot's
  own rate in the tooltip).
- "skinner" (and "miner", "herbalist"...) finds only trainers who'll teach you, as "skinning trainer" does.
- A quest several NPCs give: its distance, Shift+Enter and map pin go to one of yours, the nearest.
- "who sells pet food" takes the game's answer on what your pet eats first, as "what can my pet eat" does.
- A place in Simple mode ("vendor barrens") takes NPCs there by their zone's name too, as its Alt+` line `in:barrens`
  does.

**Other changes**
- The `trainer:` filter's help names its rank form; docs/PROVIDERS.md says how the kinds' column, its colours and
  icons are drawn for add-on authors.
- The colour filters read your professions once a frame, not once per recipe row; the kind column looks at a list's
  first 200 rows at most and keeps no list it judged.
- Translations: the new texts in German, French, Spanish, Russian and Chinese.

## 1.6.0

Terminal 1.6: auction house prices from TradeSkillMaster, DungeonJournal's pages and favorites, a setting to thank
players who buff you, the Library's reward tiers with their book counts, no freeze after login, and the fixes of a
release review.

**TradeSkillMaster prices**
- With TradeSkillMaster installed, its prices come first and Auctionator's fill in the items TSM has none for; either
  one alone gives every auction house feature ("what should i auction", "am i undercut", `sort:ahvalue`,
  `| sum ahvalue`, `is:auctionable`). Read through TSM's public `TSM_API`: its AuctionDB's minimum buyout, else its
  market value. TSM's prices come from its desktop app.
- `@auction`'s undercut compares your price with what's up now: TSM's minimum buyout (never its 14-day market value)
  or Auctionator's last scan. Each price says whose it is, and "prices from ..." names the addons behind the rows
  shown.
- A copy with a random suffix ("of the Bear") gets a price only from a source that has that copy's own.
- Prices are asked again 10 s after logging in: TSM reads its data after Terminal has loaded.
- The install hints and `.integrations` name both addons, TSM first.

**DungeonJournal**
- With DungeonJournal installed, a row's right-click menu has "Show in Dungeon Journal" whenever it lists the thing:
  an item (a boss's loot or a quest's reward) opens on its page with the item pointed at, a quest on its quest page, a
  dungeon (`@dungeon`) on its own page, on any client language.
- `@favorite` (also `@favourite`, `@favs`, `@fav`): the items you starred in the journal, with the boss or quest each
  comes from. "my favorites" and "dungeon journal favorites" (or "favourites") ask for them; `is:favorite` finds them
  among items, loot and gear too.
- Read through the namespace it keeps as a global, every part checked: a version without one says so once, as every
  integration does, and on its `.integrations` line.

**Thank players who buff you**
- A new setting (`.set thankBuffs on`, or in "terminal settings"), off unless you turn it on: a /thank to a player
  outside your group whose buff (one lasting over a minute) lands on you, each player at most once in 10 minutes.
- Never while the game restricts addons (combat, a boss fight, a keystone dungeon, a PvP match), and never for buffs
  the game reports again after a loading screen or a `/reload`.
- With OneForAll's own "Thank players who buff you" on, Terminal leaves it to OneForAll, as that option is set now.

**Library Books**
- "library book rewards" without OneForAll lists only the Library's three reward tiers, each with how many books it
  takes (on every client language); other librarians' quests were listed by mistake.

**Other changes**
- No short freeze half a minute after logging in: the list of recipes you haven't learned was built in one frame
  (0.2 s with 584 recipes). What Questie says of each recipe's item is now kept for the session and read ahead a few
  milliseconds a frame.
- `is:`'s help names `is:favorite`; `@favorite` has a colour of its own.
- For add-on authors: a list's `prewarm` (docs/PROVIDERS.md) reads ahead of its first build through
  `Terminal.Integrations.RunSliced`.
- 20 new texts translated (German, French, Spanish, Russian, Chinese).

New files: restart the game, not just `/reload`.

## 1.5.0

Terminal 1.5: Library Books and item sets without OneForAll (from Questie and AtlasLoot), a tidier `.integrations`, the
Legacy innkeeper on every client language, faster close spellings and read-ahead, and the fixes of a release review.

**Library Books without OneForAll**
- `@book` with Questie or the QuestieDB addon alone: QuestieDB's own data has WoW Forever's 40 Library Books, read
  while it's installed, never copied: each book's quest (its name, in the client's language), the item, and the world
  object it lies in with its spot (a second zone's spot said as "Also found at"). No list is kept: a book is told by
  its shape among QuestieDB's quests (started by a world object and by an NPC titled "Librarian", or of the Special
  sort with the item it asks for lying in that object; the sort as QuestieDB's base data has it, `Quest.GetRaw`: its
  WoW Forever corrections move the Library quests to your capital). "library books", "books i still need",
  "nearest library book", `is:todo` / `is:done` and Enter's waypoint work as with OneForAll; how far along you are is
  the game's own answer. QuestieDB's quests are read a slice a frame after Questie's own indexing, asked again until
  they can be.
- **library book rewards** lists each reward as an item's own row under its tier (the item's tooltip, its colour,
  Enter as any item). Without OneForAll: the Librarians' reward quests and the items Questie says they give,
  "(claimed)" once turned in; how many books each takes is OneForAll's to say.
- OneForAll's list still comes first when it's installed (a note on each spot, the sets, the reward tiers, books you
  marked done).

**Item sets without OneForAll**
- `@itemset` with AtlasLoot alone: its public set data (`AtlasLoot.Data.ItemSet`), read while it's installed. The sets
  are those of the items in its loot list; a set's name is the game's, its pieces' slots the game's words, where a
  piece comes from its loot rows' boss and place, its bonuses AtlasLoot's lines. Worked out once per AtlasLoot index
  (read ahead while idle); a piece's name is asked for when shown.
- Enter opens AtlasLoot on the page that lists the set, points at it and shows its items, as a click on it does;
  Shift+Enter lists its pieces in Terminal. Where each set is listed is noted with AtlasLoot's index (built again once).
- Whose a set is: AtlasLoot's own set icon for its raid and PvP sets; the dungeon sets, which its data marks with no
  class, by the column AtlasLoot's set pages lay each class in (learned from the pages whose every set it marks, given
  only on pages that fill exactly those columns: the 18 dungeon sets, as its data file's notes say). "my class sets",
  `class:` and "pieces of " work as with OneForAll, whose list still comes first.

**`.integrations`**
- Lists only the addons Terminal found (one installed that failed to start still says so, with why; none: "none").
- The enchants, the Library Books and the item sets get a line each, saying how many and from which addon
  ("Enchants: 312 (`@enchant`): 290 from AtlasLoot, 22 more from OneForAll"); OneForAll's line keeps its factions'
  rewards.

**Other changes**
- Legacy rewards: Innkeeper Wiley is found by QuestieDB's untranslated name on a client in another language (QuestieDB
  translates names there), so Enter on a reward has its waypoint.
- Close spellings of a long word in under half the time: a word is measured only when enough of the typed letters are
  in it (20,000 names: 150-180 ms became 55-70 ms, the same words found).
- Read ahead while idle, a slice a frame: a hunter's pet foods and the loot's tokens and item sets, also when a search
  built their list first; asked for before that's done, the rest is read at once.
- The install hints name the right addon: "OneForAll or Questie" for `@book`, "OneForAll or AtlasLoot" for
  `@itemset` and `> pieces` (OneForAll's parts shared one name, so only the last counted).
- Wording: a book with no spot says "show in chat"; rewards say "Lv N"; a malformed OneForAll books or sets table
  says the other addon's are used instead.
- Under the hood: one shared helper each for spell and item names, your class and the chat-box pair; the four largest
  files split (`Providers/MailRows.lua`, `Search/Steps/ChainLearn.lua` and `ChainRun.lua`,
  `Search/Questions/QuestUpgrades.lua` and `QuestFacts.lua`, `UI/BarMenu.lua`).
- `tests/gen_data.py --check` passes again: the cooking fires' marker line had been merged into a comment.

New files: restart the game, not just `/reload`. AtlasLoot's loot index is built again once.
